taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the clump of arching leaves 0.6 m to 1 m high, as in the photos; the leaves are 80-130 cm long (FNA).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Nolina microcarpa: flowers are arranged in a panicle supported by a stout stem that may reach 5.9 feet (1.8 m) tall.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Nolina microcarpa: an erect to spreading perennial shrub or large forb; life span may be less than 50 years.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: plants acaulescent, cespitose; rosettes from vertical, subterranean, branched caudices.

traits.clonal.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: cespitose, rosettes from branched caudices; it forms large clumps up to 2 m in diameter.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves live several years, the dead ones staying in the clump.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: leaf blades wiry, lax, concavo-convex; a fountain of arching leaves in the photos.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: leaf blades 80-130 cm x 5-12 mm; FEIS: 0.5-1.2 m long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: leaf blades 80-130 cm x 5-12 mm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: leaf blades wiry, 80-130 cm x 5-12 mm: linear.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: margins serrulate, with close-set, cartilaginous teeth.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: leaf blades not glaucous; dull green in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: inflorescences paniculate, 4-12 dm x 10-30 cm, surpassing leaves.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: inflorescences paniculate, 4-12 dm x 10-30 cm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: tepals white, 1.5-3.3 mm.

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS species review, Nolina microcarpa: Southwestern Nolina species are primarily dioecious; FNA lists fertile and infertile stamens.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: capsules hyaline, thin-walled, inflated.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: capsules 4.2-6 x 5.4-6.4 mm.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 416, 418, 419 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Nolina microcarpa: capsules 4.2-6 x 5.4-6.4 mm.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS species review, Nolina microcarpa: sacahuista flowers in mid- to late spring (May-June) throughout its range; Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 199): May and June.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe June to August.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for beargrass from Flora of North America vol. 26 and FEIS (Gucker 2007): an acaulescent clump (trunk_rate 0) of many wiry, lax leaves 80-130 cm long (leaf_length 1.0, each 10% either way), spreading from the centre (young_angle 50, old_angle 80, angle_spread 4) so the clump stands about 0.9 m, cespitose from branched caudices to 2 m across (pups 4, their leaves starting near full size, leaf_seed 0.8, as offsets of an old caudex do), the caudex barely raised (internode 0.00005), the dead leaves kept in the clump as the photos show (skirt 1), a panicle 4-12 dm on a scape (stalk_height 0.7, stalk_head 0.5, so a flowering clump stays near its usual height), tiny white flowers 2-5 to a node (flowers 40 a branch). The blade's aspect is at its least, 0.01 (true 0.008); leaf rate, bloom and flower_age are estimates.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense fountain of long, wiry, arching grass-like leaves with straw-coloured dead ones among them, and tall wands of tiny cream flowers rising above in late spring.

allometry.note: 1.0 m tall at 15 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
